title: The Best Mars Photos Taken by the Curiosity Rover
gist: The Curiosity rover marked 14 years on Mars on Aug. 6, 2026, approaching 5,000 sols of operation against an original commission of only a couple of years, and remains fully operational and in contact with Earth. Short anniversary photo-gallery intro.

themes.theme: Hardware vastly outliving its design life

insights.claim: The Curiosity rover landed on Mars on Aug. 6, 2012 and had operated for exactly 14 years as of this piece, approaching 5,000 sols of surface operation.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Concrete mission-duration benchmark for judging planetary hardware lifetime assumptions.
insights.locator: The Curiosity rover has been trundling around Mars

insights.claim: Curiosity was originally commissioned to work on the Martian surface for only a couple of years, so its realized lifetime exceeds its planned lifetime by roughly seven times.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Amortized cost per operating year for flagship planetary missions runs far below the figure implied at approval.
insights.quote: having only originally been commissioned to work on the Martian surface for a couple of years

insights.claim: Despite a few knocks and scrapes, the 1,982-pound rover is still fully operational and still communicating with Earth after 14 years of Martian conditions.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Evidence that radioisotope-powered, conservatively engineered surface hardware degrades gracefully rather than failing at design life.
insights.quote: We owe a lot to this 1,982-pound buggy
insights.locator: still fully operational (albeit with a few knocks and scrapes)
